metas.name: After Life
metas.description:
Captures the dead choosing one memory to keep forever, processed by a calm office of caseworkers who stage and film each chosen moment. People pick afternoons, a breeze, a childhood shame redeemed. Your memory-and-projection interests in their gentlest possible form — the afterlife as an archive with a production department.

After death, people have a week to choose only one memory to keep for eternity.

metas.name: Once
metas.description:
Captures two musicians in Dublin falling into perfect collaboration and declining, kindly, to wreck their lives with it. A busker and a Czech pianist make an album in a week; the love is real, expressed entirely as music, and the ending honours everyone including the people not in the room. Shot on a camcorder for almost nothing.

A modern-day musical about a busker and an immigrant and their eventful week in Dublin, as they write, rehearse and record songs that tell their love story.

metas.name: The Lunchbox
metas.description:
Captures a connection routed through Mumbai's dabbawala lunchbox system by a one-in-a-million delivery error. A lonely accountant receives the lunch a neglected wife cooked for her husband; notes ride back inside the empty tins. Contemporary ordinary life — offices, trains, ageing in the city — with food as the medium.

A mistaken delivery in Mumbai's famously efficient lunchbox delivery system connects a young housewife to an older man in the dusk of his life as they build a fantasy world together through notes in the lunchbox.

metas.name: Happy Hour
metas.description:
Captures four women friends in Kobe, in their late thirties, at the length friendship actually takes: five hours seventeen minutes. Workshops, dinners, a hearing, a reading — one friend's decision re-sorts all four lives. The friendship film your collection barely has, made with the patience of the films it does have.

A slow-burning epic chronicling the emotional journey of four thirty something women in the misty seaside city of Kobe.

metas.name: The Station Agent
metas.description:
Captures three lonely people failing to leave each other alone. A man with dwarfism inherits a disused train depot to be solitary in; a grief-struck artist and a talkative coffee-truck man refuse the plan. Nothing is cured; company simply accumulates. Friendship as accretion, not event.

When his only friend dies, a man born with dwarfism moves to rural New Jersey to live a life of solitude, only to meet a chatty hot dog vendor and a woman dealing with her own personal loss.

metas.name: Nebraska
metas.description:
Captures a son driving his father toward a million dollars that don't exist, because the wanting is the last clear thing the old man has. Black-and-white plains, a family reunion where everyone itemises old debts, and a reconciliation with no speech in it — just a truck, a compressor, and a main street driven slowly.

An aging, booze-addled father makes the trip from Montana to Nebraska with his estranged son in order to claim a million-dollar Mega Sweepstakes Marketing prize.

metas.name: Lucky
metas.description:
Captures a 90-year-old atheist's daily routine as a complete philosophy: yoga, crosswords, a missing tortoise named President Roosevelt, the same bar, the same stool. Harry Dean Stanton's final role — old age as appetite and community rather than decline, in a desert town that has made room for him exactly as he is.

Lucky follows the spiritual journey of a 90-year-old atheist and the quirky characters that inhabit his off the map desert town.

metas.name: Billy Elliot
metas.description:
Captures a miner's son whose body insists on ballet during the strike that is crushing his father. The body in health, at last: dancing as the one articulate thing in a house of men who can't talk. And the father's thaw — pride arriving through sacrifice he never announces — is the reconciliation your list usually withholds.

A talented young boy becomes torn between his unexpected love of dance and the disintegration of his family.

metas.name: Moneyball
metas.description:
Captures competence itself as drama: a general manager and a Yale economist re-deriving baseball from its statistics while the entire sport's intuition laughs at them. The closest film on this list to your actual profession — observed numbers versus inherited scouting folklore, and the numbers are the love story.

Oakland A's general manager Billy Beane's successful attempt to assemble a baseball team on a lean budget by employing computer-generated analysis to acquire new players.

metas.name: Challengers
metas.description:
Captures a tennis match as the only honest conversation three people can have. A wife, a husband and his ex-best friend, thirteen years of desire and ambition routed through one challenger final, the camera riding the ball. Bodies in motion, erotic and athletic at once — the contemporary register the list was missing.

Tashi, a former tennis prodigy-turned-coach, transformed her husband into a champion. But to overcome a recent losing streak and redeem himself, he'll need to face off against his former best friend--Tashi's ex-boyfriend.

metas.name: This Is Spinal Tap
metas.description:
Captures a metal band's decline documented with total, lethal courtesy. Your collection holds exactly one film tagged Satire; this is the second, and it's also the music-industry film — amps to eleven, drummers expiring, a Stonehenge set built to the wrong unit. The mockumentary as a transducer problem: every interview projects a band that no longer exists.

Spinal Tap, one of England's loudest bands, is chronicled by film director Marty DiBergi on what proves to be a fateful tour.

metas.name: The Band's Visit
metas.description:
Captures an Egyptian police orchestra stranded for one night in the wrong Israeli town, and enmity dissolving into dinner, small talk and a roller rink. Reconciliation without a summit — just people feeding their assigned enemies. The quietest film here, and the one where music does diplomacy's job.

A band comprised of members of the Egyptian police force head to Israel to play at the inaugural ceremony of an Arab arts center, only to find themselves lost in the wrong town.

metas.name: Good Bye, Lenin!
metas.description:
Captures a son rebuilding East Germany in his mother's bedroom because the truth would kill her. Forged news broadcasts, decanted pickles, a whole fake state maintained as an act of love. History in your collection is usually an indictment; here it's a forgery staged by tenderness.

In 1990, to protect his fragile mother from a fatal shock after a long coma, a young man must keep her from learning that her beloved nation of East Germany as she knew it has disappeared.

metas.name: Of Gods and Men
metas.description:
Captures a monastery of French monks in Algeria deciding, by discussion and by choir, whether to stay with the village that depends on them as the violence closes in. Faith as belonging tested at the highest price — and the belonging is shown first: meals, medicine, a birthday, one bottle of wine and a tape of Swan Lake.

Under threat by fundamentalist terrorists, a group of Trappist monks stationed with an impoverished Algerian community must decide whether to leave or stay.

metas.name: Supa Modo
metas.description:
Captures a Kenyan village conspiring to give a terminally ill girl her superhero movie. Jo is nine, obsessed with action films, and going home to die; the village stages rescues, builds costumes, shoots her scenes. A community performing cinema as care — the Hara premise inverted to warmth: the camera as accomplice in a kind lie.

Story of a young girl whose dream of becoming a superhero is threatened by terminal illness, inspiring her village to rally together to make her dream come true.

metas.name: Rafiki
metas.description:
Captures two Nairobi girls — daughters of rival politicians — falling in love in saturated colour, in a country that banned the film for exactly that. Love that works as an act of local defiance; the palette alone is an argument that joy is a register, not an escape.

"Good Kenyan girls become good Kenyan wives," but Kena and Ziki long for something more. When love blossoms between them, the two girls will be forced to choose between happiness and safety.

metas.name: Mysterious Object at Noon
metas.description:
Captures a story built by handing it from stranger to stranger across Thailand: a teacher, a boxer, market sellers each continue a tale about a boy and a mysterious object, and Apichatpong films their additions as fact. Storytelling as a chain of transducers, each adding loss and invention — your framework run as a parlour game in 16mm black and white.

A camera crew travels through Thailand asking villagers to invent the next chapter of an ever-growing story.

metas.name: Ilo Ilo
metas.description:
Captures an ordinary Singapore family during the 1997 financial crisis, and the Filipina maid who becomes load-bearing in it. No villain, no collapse — a boy's jealousy slowly becoming attachment while the adults quietly fail and cope. The Family genre, done at the collection's standard.

In 90s Singapore, the friendship between Filipino nursemaid Teresa and her young charge Jiale makes waves in a family, while the Asian recession hits the region.

metas.name: Whale Rider
metas.description:
Captures a Māori girl certain she is the chief her grandfather is waiting for a boy to be. Tradition as both wound and vehicle; the reconciliation, when it comes, arrives by whale. Oceania and Indigenous belonging, carried by a twelve-year-old's total lack of doubt.

A contemporary story of love, rejection and triumph as a young Maori girl fights to fulfill a destiny her grandfather refuses to recognize.

metas.name: Son of the Bride
metas.description:
Captures a burnt-out restaurateur whose father announces he wants, at last, to marry his wife of 44 years — who has Alzheimer's — in the church wedding they never had. A son restaging his parents' love while his own life is in receivership. Mid-life repair, played warm and exact.

A dissatisfied 40-year-old, separated and without time for his own daughter and girlfriend must rethink his life when his father decides to marry his mother, who suffers from Alzheimer's disease, by church.

metas.name: Gloria
metas.description:
Captures a 58-year-old divorcée in Santiago going dancing, falling into a messy affair, and refusing to shrink. Old-er age as appetite — discos, road trips, a paintball gun used with feeling. Paulina García holds every frame; the ending is a woman dancing alone because she wants to.

A story set in Santiago and centered on Gloria, a free-spirited older woman, and the realities of her whirlwind relationship with a former naval officer whom she meets out in the clubs.

metas.name: Kiki's Delivery Service
metas.description:
Captures a thirteen-year-old witch founding a delivery business in a seaside town, and competence arriving in stages: first flights, first customers, a slump where the gift itself fails. Work as dignity, kindness of strangers as infrastructure.

Along with her black cat Jiji, Kiki settles in a seaside town and starts a high-flying delivery service. Here begins her magical encounter with independence and responsibility, making lifelong friends and finding her place in the ...

metas.name: My Neighbor Totoro
metas.description:
Captures childhood before it learns to be endangered: two sisters new to the countryside, a mother in hospital kept almost off-screen, and the forest spirits who treat worry as weather. The children's happiness here is not ignorance — it's a skill the film takes seriously.

When two girls move to the country to be near their ailing mother, they have adventures with the wondrous forest spirits who live nearby.

metas.name: The Iron Giant
metas.description:
Captures a boy teaching a fifty-foot weapon that it can choose what it is. Cold War Maine, a beatnik sculptor, a government man terrified of the unknown — and the Giant learning the word for what he refuses to be. Friendship between unequals where the smaller one does the moral teaching; “you are who you choose to be” earned, not printed.

A young boy befriends a giant robot from outer space that a paranoid government agent wants to destroy.
